headline: Explicit prior structure built into omics and clinical prediction models
label: Structured Priors In Omics
summary: Recent preprints embed longitudinal, multimodal, and similarity priors directly into omics-based disease and drug-prediction models.
synthesis: The common thread is that prior structure is encoded into the model itself rather than recovered afterward. MT-LLE builds locally linear embeddings of longitudinal COPD omics under five jointly optimized objectives, with an RL agent scheduling their weights. DeMoP recasts clinical and copy-number data as text for DeBERTa-based mixture-of-experts prognosis, reporting AUROC 0.939 on GENIE and 0.805 on TCGA. MVGCL fuses noisy multisource drug and disease similarities with type-aware dual-pathway contrastive learning for drug-disease association prediction. InsilicoCell, a pretrained multimodal transformer, departs from this pattern by targeting cellular functional profiles and multi-objective virtual drug screening. The thread is dominant rather than uniform. What is new is explicit encoding of longitudinal, modality, and similarity relations into the learning objective or representation.
